The sun casts an orange light across the dusk sky as a figure trudges through the sandy wind torn dunes, a whistling wind carries the sand twirling in wisps past the peaks. Slow and seemingly weak, they slowly edge their way closer. Closer to a silent monument in the sea of dust and sand. A small refuge from the ever present etching wind.

It stands three levels tall, its shimmering grey stone a beacon in the vast dunes, open arched doorway beckoning weary wanderers for eons. A pyramid shaped roof adorns its top, arched windows peek out on the top level below it. Eloquently adorned windows in the middle, and a few ropes dangle lazily in the breeze, seemingly from previous explorations to find it.

Breaking through the open threshold with relief the figure collapses the sound of the wind now echoing in a eerie hollowness. Only now it is joined by another faint sound. Gurgling and bubbling of water manifests from the back of the stonework. Slowly as the figure notices the sound, he removes his hood revealing a grisly face of scars, deeply tanned adorned with a full and thick black beard and a messy head of long black hair.

Gingerly he gets up and makes his way towards the sound of salvation, finding it a fountain carved into the wall, with three spouts pouring a thin stream of cold clear water. Softly bubbling the streams fell into a half circle pool full to the brim of clear water, the stone keeping it cool and refreshing.

Smiling the man removes his heavy garb and boots, giggling softly at the thrill. With cupped hands he scoops water from the pool drinking deeply wiping his hands through his beard. With a heavy sigh of satisfaction he gently dips his right foot into the pool of water. Shifting his weight with a now audible laugh, he brings his other foot into the pool.

Lowering himself slowly, breathing rapidly between laughs his body tensing in the cold water shocked at the sudden change. With a small splash of water over the edge of the pool he drops his rear into the pool and sighs relaxing waving his hands through the water, floating gently to sleep.

Crickets wake him in the early dawn, shivering the man dries himself and fills his canteens. Digging through his bags he produces some packets filled with what look like bars of chocolate. Crunching a few down and packing his bags, he takes one last hand cupful of water, drinking and wiping his beard with wet hands. A small amount of sadness, and relief the man thanks the builders of this place, setting off into the dunes once again as the sun peeks its way over the horizon.
